strategy.summary: GET /products filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit`/`offset` (limit defaults to 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT), returns `{ total, items }`, and refuses non-whole-number limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. The tests start the real app on an OS-chosen port (as the existing spec does) and check search, paging, the cap and the refusals over HTTP.
inScope: GET /products query parameters q, limit, offset
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
assumptions: The cap is the code's MAX_LIMIT = 50, not the README's 100 (asked as Q1); tests import MAX_LIMIT and also check that 50 items come back.

The real app runs in-process via createApp() on port 0; nothing is faked. The catalogue is the fixed 120-product PRODUCTS list (names like 'Kettle 1'..'Kettle 15'), which the GET endpoint doesn't modify.
Items come back in catalogue (id) order, as the README says.
A negative offset ('-1') counts as not a whole number and is refused, as the code does.
openQuestions: README says limit goes up to 100 but code caps at 50: which is right? (Q1)

risks.description: Case-sensitive matching would miss products when users type in a different case
risks.mitigation: TC2 searches in upper case and checks the same matches as lower case

risks.description: total reports the page size instead of all matches, breaking pagination UI
risks.mitigation: TC4 checks total stays 15 while the page holds 5

risks.description: Unbounded limit lets a client fetch the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC5 asks for 1000 and expects exactly MAX_LIMIT items
TC6 table of invalid values each expecting 400

acceptanceCriteria.text: q returns exactly the products whose name contains it, case-insensitively; without q every product is listed.
limit and offset select a page of the matches, the response's total is the number of all matches, and limits above the maximum are capped.
limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or limit below 1, gets 400.

steps: GET /products with each of limit=abc, limit=2.5, limit=0, limit=-1, offset=abc, offset=1.5, offset=-1

testCases.rationale: Ensures the refusal boundary isn't off by one

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services. The app is started in-process on an OS-chosen port; runs with the existing `npm test`.
